newsitem.title: SPAIN: Good conditions for reducing Spain inflation - Rojo.
newsitem.headline: Good conditions for reducing Spain inflation - Rojo.

text.p: Bank of Spain governor Luis Angel Rojo said on Wednesday that conditions were favourable for reducing inflation.
In a speech to a legislative committee on the economy, Rojo also said he saw no obstacles to producer price growth beneath 2.5 percent in 1997.
"There is nothing which in principle contradicts that this component of CPI - prices of industrial goods - converges toward a growth path of below 2.5 percent throughout 1997," Rojo said.

"Current conditions in the Spanish economy are favourable to making the effort on inflation required by the monetary objectives established and to reach the goals of convergence for the European common currency," Rojo said.

Nonetheless, he called attention to the development of service sector prices. These were registering tension due to the end of the phase of salary moderation, the recovery of domestic demand, and employment growth.

"If the rhythm of growth of this component remains at present rates the progress that can be made in the reduction of overall inflation will be limited and will probably be insufficient to reach the goals drawn out," he said.
